title: Quasi-compact opens in base changes of finitely presented affine charts
statement: Let $S$ and $T$ be quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $t:T\to S$ be a morphism. Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ be an affine open subscheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], let $B$ be a finitely presented commutative $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and give $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ its composite structure map $X\to V\hookrightarrow S$. Put $X_T=X\times_ST$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every open subscheme $W\subseteq X_T$ whose underlying topological space is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], the composite $W\hookrightarrow X_T\to T$ is of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

source.place: Tags 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), 01TR (lemma-composition-finite-presentation), 01TS (lemma-base-change-finite-presentation), 01TU (lemma-quasi-compact-open-immersion-finite-presentation); applied to an affine chart and a quasi-compact open of its base change.

proof.text: Write $a:X\to V$, $j:V\hookrightarrow S$, $p:X_T\to T$ and $i:W\hookrightarrow X_T$ for the given maps. Both $j$ and $i$ are locally of finite presentation, by the following elementary argument for an open immersion $h:U\hookrightarrow Y$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], identify $U$ with its open image. For any $u\in U$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] gives an affine open $D\subseteq Y$ containing $h(u)$ and contained in that image. Its inverse image in $U$ is the same affine open subscheme, and the restricted map is the identity on $D$. The induced ring map $R\to R$ has the presentation $R=R[x_1,\ldots,x_0]/(0)$, with no variables and no relations, as in [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. These affine neighbourhoods witness finite presentation at every point in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

source.place: Tag 01TT (lemma-open-immersion-locally-finite-presentation), proof: an open immersion is a local isomorphism; affine neighbourhoods from Schemes Tag 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens).

proof.text: The schemes $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The structure map $a$ is locally of finite presentation directly from [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]: at every point take all of $X$ and all of $V$ as the affine neighbourhoods. Their global section rings and induced map are $B$, $A$ and the given algebra structure, respectively, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $B$ has the required finite presentation by hypothesis. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], with affine source $X$ and quasi-separated target $V$, now makes $a$ of finite presentation.

source.place: Definition Tag 01TP (definition-finite-presentation), pointwise affine definition; Schemes Tags 00E8/01KN for affine qcqs and 03GI/01KV for morphism permanence.

proof.text: Step 2 makes $V$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, while $S$ is quasi-separated by hypothesis. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] therefore makes $j$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Together with Step 1, this says that $j$ is of finite presentation. By clause (d) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], the composite $f=j\circ a:X\to S$ is of finite presentation. The map $p:X_T\to T$ is its base change along $t$, so clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $p$ of finite presentation. In particular $p$ is quasi-separated; since $T$ is quasi-separated, clause (2) of that same node makes $X_T$ quasi-separated.

The open immersion $i:W\hookrightarrow X_T$ is separated by clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation], hence quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Its source $W$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis and its target $X_T$ is quasi-separated by Step 3. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] consequently makes $i$ quasi-compact. Step 1 already gives local finite presentation of $i$, so it is of finite presentation. This distinguishes quasi-compactness of the space $W$ from quasi-compactness of the immersion; the latter uses the established quasi-separatedness of its target.

source.place: Tag 01TU (lemma-quasi-compact-open-immersion-finite-presentation), proof; Schemes Tag 01L7 (lemma-immersions-monomorphisms), paragraph after Definition 01KK, and Tag 03GI (lemma-quasi-compact-permanence).

proof.text: Steps 3 and 4 give finite presentation of both $p$ and $i$. Apply clause (d) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] to obtain finite presentation of $p\circ i:W\to T$. Its three properties are exactly local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, as specified in the statement.
